environment.description: Same application deployed on EKS with MongoDB Atlas M30 cluster. Vault Agent sidecar (HashiCorp Vault 1.15) injects ephemeral MongoDB Atlas credentials via database secrets engine with TTL=60s and max_ttl=60s. Atlas cluster configured with queryable-encryption-required namespace constraint on 'users' collection via Atlas Data API policy. MongoDB Atlas Advanced Security: IP Access List restricted to EKS pod CIDR only, and Atlas auditing with alerting on $where/$regex operators. Vault lease revocation is synchronous — on TTL expiry the Atlas credential is immediately removed from the Atlas user list via programmatic API callback (not lazy revocation). Additionally, the EKS pod runs with a Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate that enforces OPA policy requiring all outbound MongoDB queries to pass through a Envoy sidecar with a custom WASM filter (mongodb-query-filter v2.3.1) that parses MongoDB wire protocol and rejects any find() command containing operators $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $ne, $regex, $where, $exists, or $elemMatch unless the query originates from an allowlisted code path hash.

config.runtime: EKS 1.28, Fargate profile, pod security standard 'restricted'
config.vault: HashiCorp Vault 1.15, database secrets engine, MongoDB Atlas plugin, TTL=60s, max_ttl=60s, synchronous revocation via Atlas Admin API webhook
config.mongodb: MongoDB Atlas M30, queryable encryption namespace policy on users collection
config.network_filter: Envoy sidecar with mongodb-query-filter WASM plugin v2.3.1, blocks MongoDB operator injection at wire protocol level
config.opa_gatekeeper: ConstraintTemplate requires envoy sidecar annotation, blocks pod scheduling without filter
config.atlas_security: IP Access List: EKS pod CIDR only, audit log alerts on $where/$regex usage
config.credential_rotation: 60s TTL ephemeral credentials, synchronous Atlas user deletion on expiry
